questions.text:
If the domain of the function $f(x)=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{x^2-2x-2}\right)$, is
$(-\infty, \alpha]\cup[\beta, \gamma]\cup[\delta, \infty)$, then $\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Need $\left|\dfrac{1}{x^2-2x-2}\right|\le1$, i.e. $|x^2-2x-2|\ge1$.
$x^2-2x-2\ge1 \iff (x-3)(x+1)\ge0 \iff x\le-1$ or $x\ge3$.
$x^2-2x-2\le-1 \iff x^2-2x-1\le0 \iff 1-\sqrt2\le x\le1+\sqrt2$.
Domain $=(-\infty,-1]\cup\left[1-\sqrt2,1+\sqrt2\right]\cup[3,\infty)$, so the sum is $-1+2+3=4$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text:
Let $f$ be a function such that $3f(x)+2f\left(\dfrac{m}{19x}\right)=5x,\ x\neq0$, where
$m=\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{9}(i)^2$. Then $f(5)-f(2)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$m=\dfrac{9\cdot10\cdot19}{6}=285$, so $\dfrac{m}{19x}=\dfrac{15}{x}$.
$3f(x)+2f\left(\dfrac{15}x\right)=5x$ and, replacing $x$ by $\dfrac{15}x$, $3f\left(\dfrac{15}x\right)+2f(x)=\dfrac{75}x$.
Eliminating: $5f(x)=15x-\dfrac{150}{x}$, so $f(x)=3x-\dfrac{30}{x}$.
$f(5)-f(2)=(15-6)-(6-15)=18$.

questions.text: The smallest positive integral value of $a$, for which all the roots of $x^4-ax^2+9=0$ are real and distinct, is equal to
questions.sol:
Put $t=x^2$: $t^2-at+9=0$ must have two distinct positive roots (each gives two distinct real $x$).
Distinct: $a^2>36$; positive roots: sum $a>0$ (product $9>0$). So $a>6$ and the smallest integer is 7.

questions.text:
Let $P=[p_{ij}]$ and $Q=[q_{ij}]$ be two square matrices of order 3 such that
$q_{ij}=2^{(i+j-1)}p_{ij}$ and $\det(Q)=2^{10}$. Then the value of $\det(\operatorname{adj}(\operatorname{adj}P))$ is:
questions.sol:
$q_{ij}=\dfrac12\,2^i\,p_{ij}\,2^j$, so $Q=\dfrac12DPD$ with $D=\operatorname{diag}(2,4,8)$, $\det D=64$.
$\det Q=\dfrac18\times64^2\det P=512\det P=2^{10} \Rightarrow \det P=2$.
For order 3, $\det(\operatorname{adj}(\operatorname{adj}P))=(\det P)^{(3-1)^2}=2^4=16$.

questions.text: Let $a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4$ be an A.P. of four terms such that each term of the A.P. and its common difference $l$ are integers. If $a_1+a_2+a_3+a_4=48$ and $a_1a_2a_3a_4+l^4=361$, then the largest term of the A.P. is equal to
questions.sol:
Write the terms as $12-3e,\ 12-e,\ 12+e,\ 12+3e$ with $l=2e$.
$(144-9e^2)(144-e^2)+16e^4=361 \Rightarrow 25e^4-1440e^2+20375=0 \Rightarrow e^2=25$ or $32.6$.
Integer terms need $e^2=25$, so $e=5$, $l=10$ and the terms are $-3, 7, 17, 27$.
Largest term $=27$.

questions.text:
$\left(\dfrac13+\dfrac47\right)+\left(\dfrac{1}{3^2}+\dfrac13\times\dfrac47+\dfrac{4^2}{7^2}\right)+\left(\dfrac{1}{3^3}+\dfrac{1}{3^2}\times\dfrac47+\dfrac13\times\dfrac{4^2}{7^2}+\dfrac{4^3}{7^3}\right)+\ldots$ upto infinite terms,
is equal to
questions.sol:
With $a=\dfrac13$, $b=\dfrac47$, the $n$-th bracket is $\sum_{k=0}^{n}a^{n-k}b^k$, so the whole sum is $\sum a^ib^j$ over all $i,j\ge0$ except $i=j=0$.
Sum $=\dfrac{1}{(1-a)(1-b)}-1=\dfrac{1}{\frac23\cdot\frac37}-1=\dfrac72-1=\dfrac52$.

questions.text: The letters of the word "UDAYPUR" are written in all possible ways with or without meaning and these words are arranged as in a dictionary. The rank of the word "UDAYPUR" is
questions.sol:
Letters in order: A, D, P, R, U, U, Y.
Starting with A, D, P or R: $4\times\dfrac{6!}{2!}=1440$.
U then A: $5!=120$ (total 1560). UDA then P, R or U: $3\times3!=18$ (total 1578).
UDAYP then R: $1$ word (total 1579). The next word is UDAYPUR itself, so its rank is 1580.

questions.text:
Let $X=\{x\in\mathbb{N} : 1\le x\le19\}$ and for some $a, b\in\mathbb{R}$, $Y=\{ax+b : x\in X\}$.
If the mean and variance of the elements of Y are 30 and 750, respectively, then the sum of all possible values of $b$ is
questions.sol:
For $X$: mean $10$, variance $\dfrac{19^2-1}{12}=30$.
For $Y$: $10a+b=30$ and $30a^2=750 \Rightarrow a=\pm5$.
$a=5$ gives $b=-20$; $a=-5$ gives $b=80$. Sum $=60$.

questions.text: Let the length of the latus rectum of an ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1, (a>b)$, be 30. If its eccentricity is the maximum value of the function $f(t)=-\dfrac34+2t-t^2$, then $(a^2+b^2)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$f(t)=\dfrac14-(t-1)^2$ has maximum $\dfrac14$, so $e=\dfrac14$ and $b^2=a^2\left(1-\dfrac1{16}\right)=\dfrac{15a^2}{16}$.
$\dfrac{2b^2}{a}=30 \Rightarrow \dfrac{15a}{8}=30 \Rightarrow a=16$, $b^2=240$.
$a^2+b^2=256+240=496$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text:
Let the image of parabola $x^2=4y$, in the line $x-y=1$ be $(y+a)^2=b(x-c)$,
$a, b, c\in\mathbb{N}$. Then $a+b+c$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Reflection in $x-y=1$ maps $(x,y)$ to $(y+1,\ x-1)$.
A point $(X,Y)$ is on the image when $(Y+1,\ X-1)$ is on $x^2=4y$: $(Y+1)^2=4(X-1)$.
So $a=1$, $b=4$, $c=1$ and $a+b+c=6$.

questions.text: Let the angles made with the positive $x$-axis by two straight lines drawn from the point $P(2, 3)$ and meeting the line $x+y=6$ at a distance $\sqrt{\dfrac23}$ from the point P be $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$. Then the value of $(\theta_1+\theta_2)$ is:
questions.sol:
Perpendicular distance from P to the line: $\dfrac{|2+3-6|}{\sqrt2}=\dfrac1{\sqrt2}$, along the direction at $45^\circ$.
Each line makes angle $\phi$ with that perpendicular, where $\cos\phi=\dfrac{1/\sqrt2}{\sqrt{2/3}}=\dfrac{\sqrt3}2$, so $\phi=30^\circ$.
The lines are at $45^\circ\pm30^\circ$, i.e. $75^\circ$ and $15^\circ$; sum $=90^\circ=\dfrac\pi2$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text:
The sum of all values of $\alpha$, for which the shortest distance between the lines
$\dfrac{x+1}{\alpha}=\dfrac{y-2}{-1}=\dfrac{z-4}{-\alpha}$ and $\dfrac{x}{\alpha}=\dfrac{y-1}{2}=\dfrac{z-1}{2\alpha}$ is $\sqrt{2}$, is
questions.sol:
Directions $(\alpha,-1,-\alpha)$ and $(\alpha,2,2\alpha)$; their cross product is $(0,-3\alpha^2,3\alpha)$, of length $3|\alpha|\sqrt{\alpha^2+1}$.
Joining vector $(0,1,1)-(-1,2,4)=(1,-1,-3)$; dot product with the cross product $=3\alpha^2-9\alpha$.
Distance $=\dfrac{|\alpha-3|}{\sqrt{\alpha^2+1}}=\sqrt2 \Rightarrow (\alpha-3)^2=2\alpha^2+2 \Rightarrow \alpha^2+6\alpha-7=0$.
Sum of values $=-6$.

questions.text: Let $\vec{a}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}-\hat{k}$, $\vec{b}=\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$. Let $\vec{v}$ be the vector in the plane of the vectors $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$, such that the length of its projection on the vector $\vec{c}$ is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{14}}$. Then $\left|\vec{v}\right|$ is equal to
questions.note: Official final key: all four options are accepted (the data do not fix $|\vec v|$).
questions.sol:
Let $\vec v=\lambda\vec a+\mu\vec b$. Here $\vec a\cdot\vec c=4-1-3=0$ and $\vec b\cdot\vec c=2+3-3=2$, $|\vec c|=\sqrt{14}$.
Projection: $\dfrac{|\vec v\cdot\vec c|}{\sqrt{14}}=\dfrac{2|\mu|}{\sqrt{14}}=\dfrac1{\sqrt{14}} \Rightarrow |\mu|=\dfrac12$, while $\lambda$ is not fixed.
So $|\vec v|$ is not determined by the data (for example $\mu=\dfrac12$, $\lambda=0$ gives $|\vec v|=\dfrac{\sqrt{11}}2$, which is not even listed); this is why every option is accepted.

questions.text:
Let $\vec{a}=2\hat{i}-5\hat{j}+5\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$. If $\vec{c}$ is a vector such that
$2\left(\vec{a}\times\vec{c}\right)+3\left(\vec{b}\times\vec{c}\right)=\vec{0}$ and $\left(\vec{a}-\vec{b}\right)\cdot\vec{c}=-97$, then $\left|\vec{c}\times\hat{k}\right|^2$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$(2\vec a+3\vec b)\times\vec c=\vec0$, so $\vec c=t(2\vec a+3\vec b)=t(7,-13,19)$.
$(\vec a-\vec b)\cdot\vec c=t(1,-4,2)\cdot(7,-13,19)=97t=-97 \Rightarrow t=-1$, $\vec c=(-7,13,-19)$.
$|\vec c\times\hat k|^2=c_x^2+c_y^2=49+169=218$.

questions.text:
Let $[t]$ denote the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$. If the function
$f(x)=\begin{cases}b^2\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\left[\dfrac{\pi}{2}(\cos x+\sin x)\cos x\right]\right), & x<0\\ \dfrac{\sin x-\frac12\sin2x}{x^3}, & x>0\\ a, & x=0\end{cases}$
is continuous at $x=0$, then $a^2+b^2$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Right limit: $\dfrac{\sin x(1-\cos x)}{x^3}\to1\times\dfrac12=\dfrac12$, so $a=\dfrac12$.
Left limit: for small $x<0$, $(\cos x+\sin x)\cos x=\cos^2x+\sin x\cos x$ is just below 1, so $\dfrac\pi2(\ldots)$ is just below $1.57$ and its greatest integer is 1.
Left limit $=b^2\sin\dfrac\pi2=b^2=\dfrac12$.
$a^2+b^2=\dfrac14+\dfrac12=\dfrac34$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text:
Consider the following three statements for the function $f:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ defined by $f(x)=|\log_e x|-|x-1|$:
(I) $f$ is differentiable at all $x>0$.
(II) $f$ is increasing in $(0, 1)$.
(III) $f$ is decreasing in $(1, \infty)$.
Then.
questions.sol:
On $(0,1)$: $f=-\ln x-1+x$, $f'=1-\dfrac1x<0$, so $f$ decreases: (II) is false.
On $(1,\infty)$: $f=\ln x-x+1$, $f'=\dfrac1x-1<0$: (III) is true.
At $x=1$ both one-sided derivatives are 0, so $f$ is differentiable everywhere: (I) is true.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text:
Let $f(x)=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{7x^{10}+9x^8}{\left(1+x^2+2x^9\right)^2}dx$, $x>0$, $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}f(x)=0$ and $f(1)=\dfrac14$.
If $A=\begin{bmatrix}0&0&1\\ \frac14&f'(1)&1\\ \alpha^2&4&1\end{bmatrix}$ and $B=\operatorname{adj}(\operatorname{adj}A)$ be such that $|B|=81$, then $\alpha^2$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$f'(1)=\dfrac{7+9}{(1+1+2)^2}=1$.
$|A|=1\times\left(\dfrac14\times4-1\times\alpha^2\right)=1-\alpha^2$.
For order 3, $|\operatorname{adj}(\operatorname{adj}A)|=|A|^4=81 \Rightarrow |A|=\pm3 \Rightarrow \alpha^2=4$ (the other value, $-2$, is impossible).
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text:
Let $f(\alpha)$ denote the area of the region in the first quadrant bounded by
$x=0$, $x=1$, $y^2=x$ and $y=|\alpha x-5|-|1-\alpha x|+\alpha x^2$. Then $(f(0)+f(1))$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$\alpha=0$: $y=5-1=4$. $f(0)=\displaystyle\int_0^1\left(4-\sqrt x\right)dx=4-\dfrac23=\dfrac{10}3$.
$\alpha=1$, $0\le x\le1$: $y=(5-x)-(1-x)+x^2=4+x^2$. $f(1)=\displaystyle\int_0^1\left(4+x^2-\sqrt x\right)dx=4+\dfrac13-\dfrac23=\dfrac{11}3$.
$f(0)+f(1)=7$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text:
Let $y=y(x)$ be a differentiable function in the interval $(0,\infty)$ such that $y(1)=2$,
and $\displaystyle\lim_{t\to x}\left(\dfrac{t^2y(x)-x^2y(t)}{x-t}\right)=3$ for each $x>0$. Then $2y(2)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
The limit is $0/0$; differentiating numerator and denominator in $t$ (L'Hopital) gives $\dfrac{2xy-x^2y'}{-1}=x^2y'-2xy=3$.
So $\left(\dfrac{y}{x^2}\right)'=\dfrac{3}{x^4}$, giving $\dfrac y{x^2}=-\dfrac1{x^3}+C$; $y(1)=2 \Rightarrow C=3$.
$y=3x^2-\dfrac1x$, $y(2)=12-\dfrac12$, so $2y(2)=23$.

questions.text: Let $z=(1+i)(1+2i)(1+3i)\ldots(1+ni)$, where $i=\sqrt{-1}$. If $|z|^2=44200$, then $n$ is equal to ____
questions.sol:
$|z|^2=\displaystyle\prod_{k=1}^{n}(1+k^2)=2\times5\times10\times17\times26\times\ldots$
$2\times5\times10\times17\times26=44200$, so $n=5$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let S be a set of 5 elements and P(S) denote the power set of S. Let E be an event of choosing an ordered pair (A, B) from the set $P(S)\times P(S)$ such that $A\cap B=\emptyset$. If the probability of the event E is $\dfrac{3^p}{2^q}$, where $p, q\in\mathbb{N}$, then $p+q$ is equal to __________
questions.sol:
Each element of S can be in A only, in B only, or in neither: $3^5$ favourable pairs out of $(2^5)^2=2^{10}$.
Probability $=\dfrac{3^5}{2^{10}}$, so $p+q=5+10=15$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $(h, k)$ lie on the circle $C : x^2+y^2=4$ and the point $(2h+1, 3k+2)$ lie on an ellipse with eccentricity $e$. Then the value of $\dfrac{5}{e^2}$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
With $X=2h+1$, $Y=3k+2$: $h=\dfrac{X-1}2$, $k=\dfrac{Y-2}3$, so $\dfrac{(X-1)^2}{16}+\dfrac{(Y-2)^2}{36}=1$.
Major axis vertical: $e^2=1-\dfrac{16}{36}=\dfrac59$, so $\dfrac5{e^2}=9$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text:
The number of elements in the set
$\{x\in[0, 180^\circ] : \tan(x+100^\circ)=\tan(x+50^\circ)\tan x\tan(x-50^\circ)\}$ is __________.
questions.sol:
$\tan(x+50^\circ)\tan(x-50^\circ)=\dfrac{\cos100^\circ-\cos2x}{\cos100^\circ+\cos2x}$. Cross-multiplying with $\dfrac{\tan(x+100^\circ)}{\tan x}$ and using compound-angle formulae:
$\cos100^\circ\sin100^\circ+\cos2x\sin(2x+100^\circ)=0 \Rightarrow \sin200^\circ+\sin100^\circ+\sin(4x+100^\circ)=0$.
$\sin200^\circ+\sin100^\circ=2\sin150^\circ\cos50^\circ=\sin40^\circ$, so $\sin(4x+100^\circ)=-\sin40^\circ$.
$4x+100^\circ=-40^\circ+360^\circ k$ or $220^\circ+360^\circ k$: $x=55^\circ,145^\circ,30^\circ,120^\circ$ in $[0,180^\circ]$, all with every tangent defined.
Number of elements $=4$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If $f(x)$ satisfies the relation $f(x)=e^x+\displaystyle\int_0^1\left(y+xe^x\right)f(y)\,dy$, then $e+f(0)$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Let $A=\displaystyle\int_0^1yf(y)\,dy$ and $B=\displaystyle\int_0^1f(y)\,dy$, so $f(x)=e^x+A+Bxe^x$.
$B=\displaystyle\int_0^1\left(e^y+A+Bye^y\right)dy=(e-1)+A+B$ (since $\int_0^1ye^y\,dy=1$), so $A=1-e$.
$f(0)=1+A=2-e$, hence $e+f(0)=2$.

questions.text:
A thin uniform rod $(X)$ of mass $M$ and length $L$ is pivoted at a height $\left(\dfrac{L}{3}\right)$ as shown in the figure. The rod is allowed to fall from a vertical position and lie horizontally on the table. The angular velocity of this rod when it hits the table top, is __________.
($g$ = gravitational acceleration)
questions.sol:
The pivot is $\dfrac L3$ from the lower end, so the centre of mass is $\dfrac L2-\dfrac L3=\dfrac L6$ above the pivot, which is level with the table top.
$I_{pivot}=\dfrac{ML^2}{12}+M\left(\dfrac L6\right)^2=\dfrac{ML^2}{9}$.
Energy: $\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac{ML^2}{9}\omega^2=Mg\dfrac L6 \Rightarrow \omega=\sqrt{\dfrac{3g}{L}}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.text: The velocity $(v)$ $-$ Distance $(x)$ graph is shown in figure. Which graph represents acceleration$(a)$ versus distance $(x)$ variation of this system?
questions.sol:
The graph is a straight line $v=v_0-kx$ ($v_0,k>0$).
$a=v\dfrac{dv}{dx}=(v_0-kx)(-k)=-kv_0+k^2x$: a straight line with positive slope, negative at $x=0$ and crossing zero where $v=0$.
That is graph (3).

questions.text: A flexible chain of mass $m$ hangs between two fixed points at the same level. The inclination of the chain with the horizontal at the two points of support is $30^\circ$. Considering the equilibrium of each half of the chain, the tension of the chain at the lowest point is __________.
questions.sol:
For one half (weight $\dfrac{mg}2$): vertical balance $T\sin30^\circ=\dfrac{mg}2 \Rightarrow T=mg$ at the support.
Horizontal balance: tension at the lowest point $T_0=T\cos30^\circ=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}mg$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
In case of vertical circular motion of a particle by a thread of length $r$ if the tension in the thread is zero at an angle $30^\circ$ shown in figure, the velocity at the bottom point $(A)$ of the circular path is
($g$ = gravitational acceleration)
questions.sol:
The point is $30^\circ$ above the horizontal, i.e. $r\sin30^\circ=\dfrac r2$ above the centre.
With zero tension, the radial component of gravity supplies the centripetal force: $mg\sin30^\circ=\dfrac{mv^2}{r} \Rightarrow v^2=\dfrac{gr}2$.
Energy from A (height $\dfrac{3r}2$ below that point): $v_A^2=v^2+2g\cdot\dfrac{3r}2=\dfrac{7gr}2$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A cubical block of density $\rho_b=600$ kg/m$^3$ floats in a liquid of density $\rho_e=900$ kg/m$^3$. If the height of block is $H=8.0$ cm then height of the submerged part is ______ cm.
questions.sol: Floating: $\rho_bH=\rho_eh \Rightarrow h=8.0\times\dfrac{600}{900}\approx5.3$ cm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: 10 mole of an ideal gas is undergoing the process shown in the figure. The heat involved in the process from $P_1$ to $P_2$ is $\alpha$ Joule ($P_1=21.7$ Pa and $P_2=30$ Pa, $C_v=21$ J/K.mol, $R=8.3$ J/mol.K). The value of $\alpha$ is __________.
questions.sol:
From $P_1$ to $P_2$ the volume stays at 1 m$^3$ (isochoric), so $Q=nC_v\Delta T$ and $nR\Delta T=V\Delta P$.
$Q=\dfrac{C_vV\Delta P}{R}=\dfrac{21\times1\times(30-21.7)}{8.3}=21$ J.

questions.text: The fifth harmonic of a closed organ pipe is found to be in unison with the first harmonic of an open pipe. The ratio of lengths of closed pipe to that of the open pipe is $5/x$. The value of $x$ is______.
questions.sol:
Closed pipe, fifth harmonic: $\dfrac{5v}{4L_c}$. Open pipe, first harmonic: $\dfrac{v}{2L_o}$.
Equal frequencies: $\dfrac{L_c}{L_o}=\dfrac52$, so $x=2$.

questions.text: A moving coil galvanometer of resistance 100 $\Omega$ shows a full scale deflection for a current of 1 mA. The value of resistance required to convert this galvanometer into an ammeter, showing full scale deflection for a current of 5 mA, is __________ $\Omega$
questions.sol: Shunt in parallel: $S=\dfrac{I_gG}{I-I_g}=\dfrac{1\times100}{5-1}=25\ \Omega$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two identical circular loops $P$ and $Q$ each of radius $r$ are lying in parallel planes such that they have common axis. The current through $P$ and $Q$ are $I$ and $4I$ respectively in clockwise direction as seen from $O$. The net magnetic field at $O$ is:
questions.sol:
O is on the axis at distance $r$ from each loop, so a current $I$ gives $B=\dfrac{\mu_0Ir^2}{2(2r^2)^{3/2}}=\dfrac{\mu_0I}{4\sqrt2r}$.
A current that looks clockwise from O gives a field at O pointing away from O along the axis, i.e. towards that loop: $\dfrac{\mu_0I}{4\sqrt2r}$ towards P and $\dfrac{4\mu_0I}{4\sqrt2r}$ towards Q.
Net: $\dfrac{3\mu_0I}{4\sqrt2r}$ towards Q.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A regular hexagon is formed by six wires each of resistance $r$ $\Omega$ and the corners are joined to the centre by wires of same resistance. If the current enters at one corner and leaves at the opposite corner, the equivalent resistance of the hexagon between the two opposite corners will be
questions.sol:
Let the entry corner be at potential $V$ and the exit corner at 0. By symmetry the centre is at $\dfrac V2$; the two corners next to the entry are at $x$ and the two next to the exit at $V-x$.
Node next to the entry: $(V-x)+(V-x-x)+\left(\dfrac V2-x\right)=0 \Rightarrow x=\dfrac{5V}{8}$.
Current leaving the entry: $2\cdot\dfrac{3V}{8r}+\dfrac{V}{2r}=\dfrac{5V}{4r}$, so $R=\dfrac45r$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Three parallel plate capacitors each with area $A$ and separation $d$ are filled with two dielectric ($k_1$ and $k_2$) in the following fashion. Which of the following is true?
$(k_1>k_2)$
questions.sol:
With $C_0=\dfrac{\epsilon_0A}{d}$:
(A): $k_1$ layer ($2k_1C_0$) in series with the split layer ($(k_1+k_2)C_0$): $C_A=\dfrac{2k_1(k_1+k_2)}{3k_1+k_2}C_0$.
(B): the same with $k_1,k_2$ swapped: $C_B=\dfrac{2k_2(k_1+k_2)}{3k_2+k_1}C_0$.
(C): two columns, each $k_1$ and $k_2$ in series: $C_C=\dfrac{2k_1k_2}{k_1+k_2}C_0$.
For example $k_1=2$, $k_2=1$: $C_A=1.71C_0$, $C_C=1.33C_0$, $C_B=1.2C_0$, and in general $C_A>C_C>C_B$ for $k_1>k_2$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A point source is kept at the center of a spherically enclosed detector. If the volume of the detector increased by 8 times, the intensity will
questions.sol: Volume $\times8$ means radius $\times2$. The same power spreads over $4\pi r^2$, so intensity $\propto\dfrac1{r^2}$ falls to $\dfrac14$: it decreases by 4 times.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Five persons $P_1$, $P_2$, $P_3$, $P_4$ and $P_5$ recorded object distance (u) and image distance (v) using same convex lens having power +5D as (25,96), (30,62), (35,37), (45,35) and (50,32) respectively. Identify correct statement
options: Readings recorded by all persons are correct
Readings recorded by $P_3$ person are incorrect
Readings recorded by $P_3$ and $P_2$ persons are incorrect
Readings recorded by $P_4$ and $P_5$ persons are incorrect
questions.sol:
$f=\dfrac{100}{5}=20$ cm, so for a real image $\dfrac1u+\dfrac1v=\dfrac1{20}$ (distances in cm, taken positive).
Expected $v$: $u=25\to100$, $30\to60$, $35\to46.7$, $45\to36$, $50\to33.3$.
All readings are close except $P_3$ (37 cm against 46.7 cm), so only $P_3$ is incorrect.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In the Young's double slit experiment the intensity produced by each one of the individual slits is $I_0$. The distance between two slits is 2 mm . The distance of screen from slits is 10 m. The wavelength of light is 6000 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$. The intensity of light on the screen in front of one of the slits is __________.
questions.sol:
In front of a slit, $y=\dfrac d2=1$ mm, so path difference $=\dfrac{yd}{D}=\dfrac{10^{-3}\times2\times10^{-3}}{10}=2\times10^{-7}$ m $=\dfrac\lambda3$.
Phase difference $\phi=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$, so $I=4I_0\cos^2\dfrac\phi2=4I_0\times\dfrac14=I_0$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Distance between an object and three times magnified real image is 40 cm. The focal length of the mirror used is ______ cm.
questions.sol:
A magnified real image needs a concave mirror, with object and image on the same side: $|v|=3|u|$ and $|v|-|u|=40$ cm, so $u=-20$ cm, $v=-60$ cm.
$\dfrac1f=\dfrac1v+\dfrac1u=-\dfrac1{60}-\dfrac1{20}=-\dfrac1{15}$, so $f=-15$ cm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
When a light of a given wavelength falls on a metallic surface the stopping potential for photoelectrons is 3.2 V. If a second light having wavelength twice of first light is used, the stopping potential drops to 0.7 V. The wavelength of first light is ______ m.
($h=6.63\times10^{-34}$ J.s, $e=1.6\times10^{-19}$ C, $c=3\times10^8$ m/s)
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}-\phi=3.2$ eV and $\dfrac{hc}{2\lambda}-\phi=0.7$ eV; subtracting, $\dfrac{hc}{2\lambda}=2.5$ eV, so $\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}=5$ eV $=8\times10^{-19}$ J.
$\lambda=\dfrac{6.63\times10^{-34}\times3\times10^8}{8\times10^{-19}}\approx2.5\times10^{-7}$ m.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text:
The binding energy for the following nuclear reactions are expressed in MeV.
$\mathrm{{}_2He^3+{}_0n^1\rightarrow{}_2He^4+20\ MeV}$
$\mathrm{{}_2He^4+{}_0n^1\rightarrow{}_2He^5-0.9\ MeV}$
If $X_3$, $X_4$, $X_5$ denote the stability of $\mathrm{{}_2He^3}$, $\mathrm{{}_2He^4}$ and $\mathrm{{}_2He^5}$, respectively, then the correct order is :
questions.sol:
Adding a neutron to He-3 releases 20 MeV, so $BE(\mathrm{He^4})=BE(\mathrm{He^3})+20$ MeV.
Adding a neutron to He-4 absorbs 0.9 MeV, so $BE(\mathrm{He^5})=BE(\mathrm{He^4})-0.9$ MeV $=BE(\mathrm{He^3})+19.1$ MeV.
Higher binding energy means greater stability: $X_4>X_5>X_3$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Identify the correct truth table of the given logic circuit.
questions.sol:
The upper AND gate has both inputs at A, so its output is A. The NAND gate gives $\overline{AB}$, and the next AND gate (inputs joined) passes it on.
$Y=A\cdot\overline{AB}=A\overline{B}$: Y = 1 only for A = 1, B = 0.
Table: 0, 0, 1, 0, which is option (3).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The reading of the ammeter $(A)$ in steady state in the following circuit (assuming negligible internal resistance of the ammeter) is ________ A.
questions.sol:
In steady state no current flows in the capacitor branch (so its 8 $\Omega$ carries none).
The two right-hand 8 $\Omega$ resistors are in parallel (4 $\Omega$), in series with 4 $\Omega$: 8 $\Omega$, which is in parallel with the 8 $\Omega$ next to the battery: 4 $\Omega$.
Total $=1+4=5\ \Omega$, battery current $=2$ A, which splits equally; the 1 A through the right-hand part returns through the ammeter.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A point charge $q=1\ \mu$C is located at a distance 2 cm from one end of a thin insulating wire of length 10 cm having a charge $Q=24\ \mu$C, distributed uniformly along its length, as shown in figure. Force between $q$ and wire is ______ N.
(Use : $\dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}=9\times10^9$ N.m$^2$/C$^2$)
questions.sol:
For a uniform rod of charge $Q$, length $L$, with the point charge on its line at distance $a$ from the near end: $F=\dfrac{kqQ}{a(a+L)}$.
$F=\dfrac{9\times10^9\times10^{-6}\times24\times10^{-6}}{0.02\times0.12}=\dfrac{0.216}{0.0024}=90$ N.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: When 300 J of heat given to an ideal gas with $C_p=\dfrac72R$ its temperature raises from 20 $^\circ$C to 50 $^\circ$C keeping its volume constant. The mass of the gas is (approximately) ______ g. (R = 8.314 J/mol.K)
questions.note: Dropped in the official final key (marks to all). The molar mass of the gas is not given, so the mass cannot be found; the value shown assumes $\mathrm{N_2}$ and is for reference only.
questions.sol:
At constant volume $Q=nC_v\Delta T$ with $C_v=C_p-R=\dfrac52R$.
$n=\dfrac{300}{2.5\times8.314\times30}\approx0.48$ mol.
The mass needs the molar mass, which is not given; for a diatomic gas such as $\mathrm{N_2}$ (28 g mol$^{-1}$) it would be about 13.5 g.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A soap bubble of surface tension 0.04 N/m is blown to a diameter of 7 cm. If $(15000-x)$ $\mu$J of work is done in blowing it further to make its diameter14 cm, then the value of $x$ is ______.
($\pi=22/7$)
questions.sol:
A soap film has two surfaces: $W=T\times2\times4\pi\left(R_2^2-R_1^2\right)$.
$W=0.04\times8\times\dfrac{22}7\times\left(0.07^2-0.035^2\right)=0.04\times8\times\dfrac{22}7\times0.003675=3.696\times10^{-3}$ J $=3696\ \mu$J.
$15000-x=3696 \Rightarrow x=11304$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A uniform solid cylinder of length $L$ and radius $R$ has moment of inertia about its axis equal to $I_1$. A small co-centric cylinder of length $L/2$ and radius $R/3$ carved from this cylinder has moment of inertia about its axis equals to $I_2$. The ratio $I_1/I_2$ is ______.
questions.sol:
$I=\dfrac12MR^2$ with $M\propto LR^2$, so $I\propto LR^4$.
$\dfrac{I_1}{I_2}=\dfrac{LR^4}{\frac L2\left(\frac R3\right)^4}=2\times81=162$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.text: In a meter bridge experiment to determine the value of unknown resistance, first the resistances 2 $\Omega$ and 3 $\Omega$ are connected in the left and right gaps of the bridge and the null point is obtained at a distance $l$ cm from the left. Now when an unknown resistance $x$ $\Omega$ is connected in parallel to 3 $\Omega$ resistance, the null point is shifted by 10 cm to the right of wire. The value of unknown resistance $x$ is ______ $\Omega$.
questions.sol:
$\dfrac23=\dfrac{l}{100-l} \Rightarrow l=40$ cm. New balance at 50 cm: $\dfrac{2}{R'}=1 \Rightarrow R'=2\ \Omega$.
$\dfrac{3x}{3+x}=2 \Rightarrow x=6\ \Omega$.

questions.text: One mole of $\mathrm{Cl_2(g)}$ was passed into 2 L of cold 2M KOH solution. After the reaction, the concentrations of $\mathrm{Cl^-}$, $\mathrm{ClO^-}$ and $\mathrm{OH^-}$ are respectively (assume volume remains constant)
questions.sol:
Cold dilute alkali: $\mathrm{Cl_2+2OH^-\rightarrow Cl^-+ClO^-+H_2O}$ (disproportionation).
KOH present: 4 mol; 1 mol $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ uses 2 mol, leaving 2 mol $\mathrm{OH^-}$ and forming 1 mol each of $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ and $\mathrm{ClO^-}$.
In 2 L: 0.5 M, 0.5 M, 1 M.

questions.text: The wavelength of spectral line obtained in the spectrum of $\mathrm{Li^{2+}}$ ion, when the transition takes place between two levels whose sum is 4 and difference is 2, is
questions.sol:
$n_1+n_2=4$, $n_2-n_1=2$, so the levels are 1 and 3.
$\dfrac1\lambda=R_HZ^2\left(1-\dfrac19\right)=109677\times9\times\dfrac89=877416$ cm$^{-1}$, so $\lambda\approx1.14\times10^{-6}$ cm.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Pair of species among the following having same bond order as well as paramagnetic character will be-
questions.sol:
Bond orders (MO theory): $\mathrm{O_2^+}$ 2.5, $\mathrm{O_2^-}$ 1.5, $\mathrm{N_2^+}$ 2.5, $\mathrm{N_2^-}$ 2.5, $\mathrm{N_2^{2-}}$ 2.
$\mathrm{O_2^+}$ and $\mathrm{N_2^-}$ both have bond order 2.5 and one unpaired electron (paramagnetic).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The heat of atomisation of methane and ethane are 'x' kJ mol$^{-1}$ and 'y' kJ mol$^{-1}$ respectively. The longest wavelength $(\lambda)$ of light capable of breaking the C$-$C bond can be expressed in SI unit as:
questions.sol:
C$-$H bond enthalpy $=\dfrac x4$; ethane: $\mathrm{C-C}+6\times\dfrac x4=y$, so C$-$C $=y-\dfrac{3x}{2}$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.
Energy per bond $=\dfrac{1000\left(y-\frac{3x}2\right)}{N_A}$ J $=\dfrac{250(4y-6x)}{N_A}$ J.
$\lambda=\dfrac{hc}{E}=\dfrac{N_Ahc}{250(4y-6x)}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
At 298 K, the mole percentage of $\mathrm{N_2(g)}$ in air is 80%. Water is in equilibrium with air at a pressure of 10 atm. What is the mole fraction of $\mathrm{N_2(g)}$ in water at 298 K?
($K_H$ for $\mathrm{N_2}$ is $6.5\times10^7$ mm Hg)
questions.sol:
$p_{\mathrm{N_2}}=0.8\times10$ atm $=8\times760=6080$ mm Hg.
Henry's law: $x=\dfrac{p}{K_H}=\dfrac{6080}{6.5\times10^7}\approx9.35\times10^{-5}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Two liquids A and B form an ideal solution at temperature T K. At T K, the vapour pressures of pure A and B are 55 and 15 kN m$^{-2}$ respectively. What is the mole fraction of A in solution of A and B in equilibrium with a vapour in which the mole fraction of A is 0.8?
questions.sol: $y_A=\dfrac{55x_A}{55x_A+15(1-x_A)}=0.8 \Rightarrow 55x_A=32x_A+12 \Rightarrow x_A=\dfrac{12}{23}\approx0.5217$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following gaseous equilibrium in a closed container of volume 'V' at T(K).
$\mathrm{P_2(g)+Q_2(g)\rightleftharpoons2PQ(g)}$
2 moles each of $\mathrm{P_2(g)}$, $\mathrm{Q_2(g)}$ and PQ(g) are present at equilibrium. Now one mole each of '$\mathrm{P_2}$' and '$\mathrm{Q_2}$' are added to the equilibrium keeping the temperature at T(K). The number of moles of $\mathrm{P_2}$, $\mathrm{Q_2}$ and PQ at the new equilibrium, respectively, are
questions.sol:
$K=\dfrac{2^2}{2\times2}=1$ (moles can be used as $\Delta n_g=0$).
After adding: 3, 3, 2. Let $z$ mol of $\mathrm{P_2}$ react: $\dfrac{(2+2z)^2}{(3-z)^2}=1 \Rightarrow 2+2z=3-z \Rightarrow z=\dfrac13$.
New moles: $\dfrac83, \dfrac83, \dfrac83\approx2.67$ each.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The correct order of C, N, O and F in terms of second ionisation potential is
questions.sol:
The second electron is removed from $\mathrm{C^+}$ ($2p^1$), $\mathrm{N^+}$ ($2p^2$), $\mathrm{O^+}$ ($2p^3$, half-filled, extra stable) and $\mathrm{F^+}$ ($2p^4$).
Values (kJ mol$^{-1}$): C 2353, N 2856, F 3374, O 3388. So C < N < F < O.

questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text: Choose the INCORRECT statement
options: Carbon cannot exceed its covalency more than four.
Carbon exhibits negative oxidation states along with +4 and +2.
Among the isotopes of carbon, $^{13}$C is a radioactive isotope.
$\mathrm{CO_2}$ is the most acidic oxide among the dioxides of group of 14 elements.
questions.sol:
Carbon has no d orbitals in its valence shell, so its covalency is limited to four (true). It shows $-4$ to $+4$, including $+2$ (true). $\mathrm{CO_2}$ is the most acidic group 14 dioxide (true).
$^{13}$C is a stable isotope; the radioactive one is $^{14}$C. So statement (3) is incorrect.

questions.text: "X" is an oxoanion of the lightest element of group 7 (in the periodic table). The metal is in +6 oxidation state in "X". The color of the potassium salt of X is
questions.sol: The lightest group 7 element is Mn. Its +6 oxoanion is manganate, $\mathrm{MnO_4^{2-}}$; potassium manganate, $\mathrm{K_2MnO_4}$, is green (permanganate, +7, is purple).

questions.text:
The wavelength of light absorbed for the following complexes are in the order
$\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}$ (I) ; $\mathrm{[Co(H_2O)_6]^{3+}}$ (II) ; $\mathrm{[Co(CN)_6]^{3-}}$ (III) ; $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5(H_2O)]^{3+}}$ (IV) ; $\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}$ (V)
questions.sol:
Absorbed wavelength is inversely related to the crystal-field splitting, which follows the spectrochemical series $\mathrm{CN^->NH_3>H_2O>F^-}$.
Splitting: III > I > IV (mixed $\mathrm{NH_3}$/$\mathrm{H_2O}$) > II > V, so wavelength: III < I < IV < II < V.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Find out the statements which are not true.
A. Resonating structures with more number of covalent bonds and lesser charge separation are more stable.
B. In electromeric effect, an unsaturated system shows +E effect with nucleophile and $-$E effect with electrophile.
C. Inductive effect is responsible for high melting point, boiling point and dipole moment of polar compounds.
D. The greater the number of alkyl groups attached to the doubly bonded carbon atoms, higher is the heat of hydrogenation.
E. Stability of carbanion increases with the increase in s $-$ character of the carbon carrying the negative charge.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A, C and E are true.
B is not true: the +E effect operates when the attacking reagent is an electrophile, and the $-$E effect with a nucleophile (the statement reverses them).
D is not true: more alkyl groups on the C=C make the alkene more stable, so its heat of hydrogenation is lower.
Not true: B and D only.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: There are several conformers for n$-$butane. Out of those conformers, (X), shown below, is the least stable and most stable conformer is (Y), shown below.
Statement II: As the dihedral angle increases, torsional strain decreases from (X) to (Y).
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
(X) is the fully eclipsed form (the two $\mathrm{CH_3}$ groups eclipsed, dihedral angle $0^\circ$), the least stable; (Y) is the anti form ($180^\circ$), the most stable: Statement I is true.
Going from the eclipsed $0^\circ$ form to the $180^\circ$ anti form, torsional strain falls: Statement II is true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Cross aldol condensation between two different aldehydes will always produce four different products.
Statement II: When semicarbazide reacts with a mixture of benzaldehyde and acetophenone under optimum pH, it forms a condensation product with acetophenone only.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I is false: four products form only when both aldehydes have $\alpha$-hydrogens; if one has none (e.g. HCHO or PhCHO) fewer products form.
Statement II is false: benzaldehyde, the more reactive carbonyl compound, also forms a semicarbazone (it is the faster-forming product), so the product is not formed with acetophenone only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The unsaturated ether on acidic hydrolysis produces carbonyl compounds as shown below:-
$\mathrm{CH_3-CH=CH-O-CH=CH_2\xrightarrow{H_3O^{(+)}}CH_3-CH_2-CH=O}$ and $\mathrm{O=CH-CH_3}$
Based on this, predict the solution/reagent that will help to distinguish "P" and "Q" obtained in the following reaction:-
$\mathrm{CH_3-CH=CH-O-C(CH_3)=CH_2\xrightarrow[\Delta]{H_3O^{(+)}}P+Q}$
questions.sol:
Each vinylic C$-$O$-$C=C unit gives a carbonyl compound: the $\mathrm{CH_3CH=CH-O}$ side gives propanal ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CHO}$), and the $\mathrm{O-C(CH_3)=CH_2}$ side gives acetone.
Both react with $\mathrm{NaHSO_3}$ and 2,4-DNP, and neither with Lucas reagent. Only the aldehyde reduces Fehling solution (red $\mathrm{Cu_2O}$), so Fehling solution distinguishes them.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
A student has planned to prepare acetanilide from aniline using acetic anhydride.
The student has started from 9.3 g of aniline. However, the student has managed to obtain 11 g of dry acetanilide.
The % yield of this reaction is :-
questions.sol:
Aniline ($M=93$): $\dfrac{9.3}{93}=0.1$ mol, giving at most 0.1 mol acetanilide ($M=135$) $=13.5$ g.
% yield $=\dfrac{11}{13.5}\times100\approx81.5\%$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
From the following, how many compounds contain at least one secondary alcohol?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A secondary alcohol has OH on a carbon bonded to two other carbons.
(I): only $\mathrm{CH_2OH}$ groups (primary). (II): butane-1,2-diol, the CH(OH) is secondary. (III): both OH groups are on tertiary carbons.
(IV): the side-chain CH(OH) (and the ring CH(OH)) are secondary. (V): the CH(OH)$\mathrm{CH_3}$ group is secondary. (VI): two tertiary OH and one primary.
So II, IV and V: three compounds.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The dipole moment of R-CN is greater than R-NC and R-NC can undergo hydrolysis under acidic medium to produce $\mathrm{R-\overset{O}{\overset{\Vert}{C}}-OH}$.
Statement II: R-CN hydrolyses under acidic medium to produce a compound which on treatment with $\mathrm{SOCl_2}$, followed by the addition of $\mathrm{NH_3}$ gives another compound(x). This compound (x) on treatment with NaOCl/NaOH gives a product, that on treatment with $\mathrm{CHCl_3/KOH/\Delta}$ produces R-NC
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I is false: although R$-$CN has the larger dipole moment, acid hydrolysis of an isocyanide gives a primary amine and formic acid, not RCOOH.
Statement II is true: RCN $\to$ RCOOH $\to$ RCOCl $\to$ $\mathrm{RCONH_2}$ (x); Hofmann bromamide-type degradation (NaOCl/NaOH) gives $\mathrm{RNH_2}$, and the carbylamine reaction ($\mathrm{CHCl_3}$/KOH) gives RNC.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The number of possible tripeptides formed involving alanine (ala), glycine (gly) and valine (val), where no amino acid has been used more than once is:
questions.sol: Each tripeptide uses all three amino acids once, and order matters (N-terminal to C-terminal): $3!=6$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: In the Group analysis of cations, $\mathrm{Ba^{2+}}$ & $\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}$ are precipitated respectively as
questions.sol: $\mathrm{Ba^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}$ are group V cations, precipitated by ammonium carbonate (with $\mathrm{NH_4Cl/NH_4OH}$) as $\mathrm{BaCO_3}$ and $\mathrm{CaCO_3}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
A chromium complex with a formula $\mathrm{CrCl_3.6H_2O}$ has a spin only magnetic moment value of 3.87 BM and its solution conductivity corresponds to 1 : 2 electrolyte. 2.75 g of the complex solution was initially passed through a cation exchanger. The solution obtained after the process was reacted with excess of $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$. The amount of AgCl formed in the above process is ____ g. (Nearest integer)
[Given: Molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ Cr : 52; Cl: 35.5, Ag:108, O:16, H:1]
questions.sol:
A 1 : 2 electrolyte is $\mathrm{[Cr(H_2O)_5Cl]Cl_2\cdot H_2O}$ (3.87 BM: three unpaired electrons, Cr(III)).
Molar mass $=52+106.5+108=266.5$ g mol$^{-1}$, so $\dfrac{2.75}{266.5}=1.03\times10^{-2}$ mol.
The cation exchanger keeps the complex cation (with its coordinated Cl) and releases $\mathrm{H^+}$; the two ionisable $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ per formula stay in solution.
AgCl $=2\times1.03\times10^{-2}\times143.5\approx2.96\approx3$ g.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Grignard reagent RMgBr (P) reacts with water and forms a gas (Q). One gram of Q occupies 1.4 dm$^3$ at STP. (P) on reaction with dry ice in dry ether followed by $\mathrm{H_3O^+}$ forms a compound (Z). 0.1 mole of (Z) will weigh __________ g. (Nearest integer)
questions.sol:
Molar mass of Q $=\dfrac{22.4}{1.4}=16$ g mol$^{-1}$, so Q is $\mathrm{CH_4}$ and R is $\mathrm{CH_3}$.
$\mathrm{CH_3MgBr}$ with $\mathrm{CO_2}$, then $\mathrm{H_3O^+}$, gives $\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$ (Z, 60 g mol$^{-1}$).
0.1 mol weighs 6 g.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
0.25 g of an organic compound "A" containing carbon, hydrogen and oxygen was analysed using the combustion method. There was an increase in mass of $\mathrm{CaCl_2}$ tube and potash tube at the end of the experiment. The amount was found to be 0.15 g and 0.1837 g, respectively. The percentage of oxygen in compound A is ______ %. (Nearest integer)
(Given: molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ H : 1, C : 12, O : 16)
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{CaCl_2}$ absorbs water: H $=0.15\times\dfrac2{18}=0.0167$ g. Potash absorbs $\mathrm{CO_2}$: C $=0.1837\times\dfrac{12}{44}=0.0501$ g.
O $=0.25-0.0167-0.0501=0.1832$ g, i.e. $\dfrac{0.1832}{0.25}\times100\approx73\%$.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text:
Molar conductivity of a weak acid HQ of concentration 0.18 M was found to be 1/30 of the molar conductivity of another weak acid HZ with concentration of 0.02 M. If $\lambda^\circ_{\mathrm{Q^-}}$ happened to be equal with $\lambda^\circ_{\mathrm{Z^-}}$, then the difference of the $\mathrm{p}K_a$ values of the two weak acids $(\mathrm{p}K_a(\mathrm{HQ})-\mathrm{p}K_a(\mathrm{HZ}))$ is ______ (Nearest integer).
[Given: degree of dissociation $(\alpha)$ << 1 for both weak acids, $\lambda^\circ$ : limiting molar conductivity of ions]
questions.sol:
Equal $\Lambda^\circ$ for both acids, so $\alpha=\dfrac{\Lambda_m}{\Lambda^\circ}$ gives $\alpha_{\mathrm{HQ}}=\dfrac{\alpha_{\mathrm{HZ}}}{30}$.
$K_a=c\alpha^2$: $\dfrac{K_a(\mathrm{HQ})}{K_a(\mathrm{HZ})}=\dfrac{0.18}{0.02}\times\dfrac1{900}=\dfrac1{100}$.
$\mathrm{p}K_a(\mathrm{HQ})-\mathrm{p}K_a(\mathrm{HZ})=\log100=2$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The half$-$life of $^{65}$Zn is 245 days. After $x$ days, 75% of original activity remained. The value of $x$ in days is ______. (Nearest integer)
(Given: log 3 = 0.4771 and log 2 = 0.3010)
questions.sol:
First-order decay: $x=\dfrac{t_{1/2}}{\log2}\log\dfrac{A_0}{A}=\dfrac{245}{0.3010}\log\dfrac43$.
$\log\dfrac43=2(0.3010)-0.4771=0.1249$, so $x=245\times\dfrac{0.1249}{0.3010}\approx101.7\approx102$ days.
questions.subject: Chemistry
